author: Ellis, S. James
title: Saipan Carolinian, one Chuukic language blended from many
notes: PhD dissertation, University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa, December 2012 (committee Kenneth L. Rehg, chair; Byron W. Bender; William D. O‘Grady; Yuko Otsuka; David L. Hanlon); details from the title page. Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (PDF in Downloads); §1.2.2 (pp. 7-13) and §3.2 (pp. 139-163) read, Tables 3-8 to 3-12 from the page images. 'Saipan Carolinian' (SpnCRL) is the southern Carolinian of Garapan, Oleai and Chalan Kanoa; Talaabog, the Carolinian of Tanapag, is left out (§1.2.3). The inventory draws on Jackson (1983), Jackson & Marck (1991) and the author's own experience with speakers (p. 141); the symbols are IPA (pp. 141-143).
